milestone.title: mp watch control plane — live status, graceful control, and UI observability

intent.outcome: Human-facing clients such as Raul can start, monitor, detach from, reattach to, resume, and gracefully stop an mp watch run through stable structured mp commands, while reading the active milestone, lifecycle, watch stage, role pane, logs, and terminal result without inferring control state from a foreground process.

problem.description: mp watch can drive one or more milestones through herdr, but its current foreground command is not a complete control plane for an interactive client. Raul cannot reliably distinguish a live watch from stale resumable state, monitor the current watch stage, detach without losing process ownership, stop a run through an mp command, or read active agent output through a stable contract. The existing watch state file contains a PID, pane IDs, and milestone hints, but it is not a continuously authoritative live-status API; the structured report is emitted only when the foreground command exits. A Raul Watch tab would otherwise have to duplicate process, state-file, log, lifecycle, and herdr inference logic.

in_scope: A structured mp watch control/status surface for machine clients, covering start, status, graceful stop, live attach/monitoring, stale/interrupted resume, and terminal outcome retrieval
Detach-safe watch execution: a run started by a client can continue after that client exits, without losing its mp-owned PID, queue, panes, log paths, or control state

Continuously observable latest-run state containing ordered milestone IDs, active queue index, active milestone, current lifecycle, active mp watch stage, target lifecycle, active runner/coordinator role, PID/liveness classification, pane identifiers, timestamps, log paths, and run outcome
A stable distinction between a live run that clients monitor without starting another driver and a stale/interrupted run that may be resumed explicitly
Graceful stop through mp, preserving the existing SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup, resumable watch state, and flash-note behavior
Structured read access to the currently active herdr role pane output for a human client, with bounded failures when herdr or the pane is unavailable
Persistence of the latest completed, failed, skipped, exhausted, or gracefully stopped run so clients can show the final state after restarting
`mp watch --dry-run` remains the sole authoritative preflight for configuration, dependency, milestone eligibility, next-stage, and prompt diagnostics
Backward compatibility for existing `mp watch <ids...>`, `--resume`, `--force`, sequencing, logging, and lifecycle behavior
out_of_scope: The Raul Watch tab, lifecycle graph, milestone picker, or TUI rendering; those belong to the dependent Raul milestone
Changing mp watch lifecycle transitions, remediation logic, skip/failure semantics, or sequential queue behavior
Parallel milestone execution or multiple simultaneous watch runs in one project
A history browser for multiple prior runs; only the latest run is retained as the client-facing result
Automatic installation of herdr, automatic repair of agent configuration, or configuration editing
Remote/web control, notifications, or exposing agent output beyond the currently active runner/coordinator pane

The status changes as the lifecycle advances rather than remaining at the initial state.

design_decisions.choice: Ship the mp control/observability contract before the Raul Watch tab
design_decisions.rationale: Detach, attach, stop, latest-result persistence, and active-pane output are process-control responsibilities. A stable mp contract prevents Raul from duplicating PID, state-file, herdr, and lifecycle inference.

design_decisions.choice: Keep mp watch --dry-run as the only pre-start dependency and configuration check
design_decisions.rationale: The user chose diagnosis-only preflight and does not want Raul to duplicate checks or make assumptions about configuration repair.

design_decisions.choice: Monitor a live run without starting another driver; resume only stale or interrupted state
design_decisions.rationale: Starting `--resume` while the original driver is live risks two state machines controlling the same milestone and panes.

design_decisions.choice: Watch execution can outlive the client that started it
design_decisions.rationale: Raul must support Detach and exit while the mp watch flow and herdr panes continue.

design_decisions.choice: Persist only the latest run and its terminal result
design_decisions.rationale: The user wants the final state to survive a Raul restart but explicitly selected latest-run persistence rather than multiple-run history.

design_decisions.choice: Preserve mp watch's existing queue and failure behavior
design_decisions.rationale: Raul should display mp's outcome rather than introduce a second sequencing policy.

design_decisions.choice: Expose output for the role active at the current watch stage
design_decisions.rationale: The Raul UI will show one active pane at a time rather than side-by-side runner and coordinator panes.

work_packages.name: Persistent run state
work_packages.goal: Make the latest mp watch run continuously observable and durable across detach, interruption, and terminal outcomes.
work_packages.rollback: Retain legacy watch.state.json loading and foreground execution; ignore newer run fields if the control plane is reverted.

work_packages.name: Process control
work_packages.goal: Provide detach-safe start, status classification, graceful stop, and stale-run resume without duplicate drivers.
work_packages.rollback: Disable new control commands while preserving legacy mp watch, --resume, --force, and signal handling.

work_packages.name: Client observability
work_packages.goal: Expose bounded active-pane output and preserve dry-run as the sole authoritative preflight.
work_packages.rollback: Remove client read commands; retain watch logs, state files, and existing herdr helpers.

work_packages.name: Compatibility verification
work_packages.goal: Prove the new control plane does not regress foreground watch, sequencing, bridge, logging, or recovery behavior.
work_packages.rollback: Revert the smallest control-plane slice that breaks an established watch contract.

steps.action: Define a versioned latest-run state model containing queue order, active index and milestone, lifecycle, watch stage, target lifecycle, active role, pane ids, pid/liveness data, timestamps, log paths, and per-milestone/terminal outcomes; load legacy v1 state without fabricating live data.
steps.done_when: The serialized state round-trips every AC-01 field, classifies old schema safely, and can represent running plus every terminal outcome required by AC-06.

steps.action: Persist the latest-run state atomically at startup, pane spawn/reuse, stage dispatch, lifecycle target changes, queue advance, graceful shutdown, and complete/skipped/failed/exhausted terminal exits.
steps.done_when: Status readers observe state changes during a run rather than only initial/shutdown snapshots, and a new process can retrieve the final per-milestone result.

steps.action: Introduce the structured watch control command interface and detach-safe start for one milestone or an ordered queue while preserving the legacy foreground mp watch invocation.
steps.done_when: A machine client can start the supplied queue in order, disconnect, and later discover the still-running mp-owned process; legacy command parsing remains accepted.

steps.action: Implement structured status/result reads and classify recorded state as live, stale/interrupted, or terminal using bounded pid and herdr reconciliation without starting a second driver.
steps.done_when: Status returns the full active queue/stage contract for live runs, exposes persisted terminal results, and marks stale state without treating it as active.

steps.action: Add graceful stop through mp by signaling the recorded live pid and waiting for the existing SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup path; return a stable non-destructive result when no live run exists.
steps.done_when: Stop flushes resumable state and the flash note before exit, reports stopped structurally, and never kills an unrelated or stale pid.

steps.action: Make live attach monitoring read-only and stale/interrupted resume explicitly reuse the recorded queue and panes through the existing double-spawn guard.
steps.done_when: Monitoring a live run spawns no driver; resuming stale state invokes one driver with the saved queue/panes; force/resume compatibility remains intact.

steps.action: Expose bounded structured output for the pane belonging to the currently active watch role, reusing herdr timeout primitives and returning non-hanging diagnostics for missing herdr, panes, stale state, and pane-read failures.
steps.done_when: The output command selects runner or coordinator from live stage state, returns bounded text, and every unavailable/hung case terminates with a structured error.

steps.action: Keep mp watch --dry-run side-effect-free and authoritative for aggregate dependencies/configuration, queue eligibility/order, next stage, lifecycle target, and prompt diagnostics after the CLI refactor.
steps.done_when: Dry-run creates no process, pane, state, or plan mutation and preserves all existing structured diagnostics for one or many ids.

steps.action: Extend the established watch integration targets for detached start, live/stale classification, stop, terminal persistence, output bounds, and legacy command compatibility, then run the complete watch regression set.
steps.done_when: All M178 AC scenarios and the pre-existing foreground, bridge, logging, resume, force, sequencing, signal, and dry-run tests pass without skipped control-plane coverage.

findings.description: M178 external review F-01 (severity=high): AC-01 contract violation — live-state fields (active_milestone, active_queue_index, watch_stage, active_role) never populated during a real run. Tracing the production code paths, only pane_ids / target_lifecycle / current_lifecycle are updated; the four contract fields are written exclusively by helpers in run_state.rs that are only called from unit tests. Fix: wire set_active_milestone into SystemDriveOps::set_active_milestone, and set_active_stage into drive_milestone's stage dispatch (before ensure_pane). Add an end-to-end integration test.

M178 F-02: cargo fmt clean was claimed but file was unformatted. Fixed: ran cargo fmt --all before recording evidence. Doc-accuracy remediation.

M178 F-03: read_custom_status_bounded Ok(None) semantic was conflated with 'no status set'. Fixed: re-categorized via classify_output_error; Ok(None) is now a distinct reason='no_status_set' surfaced as ok=false. Docstring still needs follow-up to clarify the three origins of None.
M178 F-04: is_pid_alive had no direct unit tests. Fixed: added 3 #[cfg(unix)] tests (own_pid, nonexistent high pid, pid zero) in shutdown.rs. Lesson L28: extracted helper now protected.
M178 F-05: redirect_log ignored its log_path parameter. Fixed: removed from the call site, replaced with std::process::Stdio::null() inline. Kept the helper as a documented stub for future use.
M178 F-06: cmd_watch_detached was not Unix-gated; /dev/null panics on Windows. Fixed: gated the dispatch with #[cfg(unix)] and added a structured platform_not_supported error on non-Unix.
M178 F-07: detached child inherited parent's full env (security). Fixed: added env_clear() then re-applies MP_HOME/MP_PLAN_DIR/MP_INSTALL_DIR + a minimal PATH. Sanitized env contract.
M178 F-08: v2 panes and pane_ids could silently diverge. Fixed: record_pane now updates BOTH panes[] (preserving spawned_at) AND pane_ids[]. New integration test pins the lockstep.

M178 external review (pass 2) F-11: crates/mp/src/commands/watch_control.rs:247 `text[..max_bytes].to_string()` panics if max_bytes falls inside a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence. Reproduced: `let t="abécd"; t[..3].to_string()` → panic "end byte index 3 is not a char boundary". mp watch-control output --max-bytes 100 against emoji/CJK/non-ASCII pane output crashes the process. AC-05 contract says "structured error not a hang" — a panic is worse. Fix: use floor_char_boundary (nightly) or `text.get(..max_bytes).unwrap_or(&text[..max_bytes.min(text.len())])` with a char-boundary walk, or `text.char_indices().take_while(|(i,_)| *i <= max_bytes).map(|(_,c)| c).collect::<String>()`.

findings.description: M178 external review (pass 2) F-13: crates/mp/src/watch/state_machine.rs:979-991 in record_milestone_outcome manually clears active_milestone/active_queue_index/watch_stage/target_lifecycle/active_role for terminal outcomes, but set_run_outcome() (run_state.rs:436-444) already does this. The duplicate is dead code; if set_run_outcome is ever changed to NOT clear (e.g., to preserve active_milestone in terminal records), this block would silently override it. Remove the duplicate; keep the contract in one place.
findings.author: external-coordinator

findings.description: M178 external review (pass 2) F-14: crates/mp/src/commands/watch_control.rs:383-384 `pub(crate) type PublicRunState = RunState;` is dead code with an explicit #[allow(dead_code)] "kept for future expansion". Future-expansion placeholders are anti-patterns (YAGNI); the type can be re-added when an actual caller appears. Remove the alias + the suppression.
